newsitem.title: DUBAI: Australia explores new Iran trade links - envoy.
newsitem.headline: Australia explores new Iran trade links - envoy.

text.p: Australia is exploring fresh trade links with Iran, the country's ambassador in Tehran was quoted on Monday as saying on his return from briefings in Canberra.

Ambassador Stuart Hume, called back to Canberra last week after a Berlin court implicated Iranian leaders in political murders in Germany, told Iran News daily he had briefed Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer and Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Trade Tim Fischer.

Hume, who presented his diplomatic credentials to President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani on April 5, said the Australian ministers "voiced their satisfaction, and it was decided that I should go back to Tehran".
He returned on Friday on the same flight as New Zealand ambassador Daniel Richards.
European Union states recalled their ambassadors from Tehran following the April 10 German court verdict. The ambassadors of Australia, New Zealand and Canada were also recalled.

Iran responded by suspending all pending trade agreements with New Zealand and cancelling the visit of a trade delegation from Australia. But Iran said on Saturday the return of the Australian and New Zealand ambassadors could boost ties.
"Dialogue is the best mechanism for resolving differences between adversaries," the English-language daily quoted Hume as saying.
"Irano-Australian trade favours Australia, and Iran has time and again voiced its concern at its imbalance," he said, adding that moves were afoot to equalise economic links.

"We are trying to explore fresh avenues for reciprocal cooperation with Iran," Hume was quoted as saying, mentioning mining, agriculture and sugar as areas with potential for cooperation. He said other areas included technology, traffic control mechanisms and medical supplies.
